runtime_env_vars.evidence: README: 'Set environment variable ROBO_AUTO_ASSETS=0 on the service to disable this behavior.'

readme_quotes: Python environment (recommended): use Docker: dependencies live in the image at /opt/venv (built with uv sync --frozen from pyproject.toml / uv.lock, including nvidia-curobo).

First build compiles CuRobo and takes >= 20 minutes. There is no GPU during build, so TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST is pre-seeded with common architectures (7.0;7.5;8.0;8.6;8.9;9.0+PTX) for CUDA-extension compilation.
pyproject.toml: no-build-isolation-package = ['nvidia-curobo'] (nvidia-curobo needs torch already present during build; uv handles this via extra-build-dependencies)

compose files declare graphics and video GPU capabilities so the NVIDIA Container Toolkit mounts libGLX_nvidia and friends; without them, SAPIEN ray-tracing init fails with 'failed to find a rendering device'.
git lfs install is needed before uv sync because nvidia-curobo is fetched from git (CuRobo).
ambiguities: pyproject.toml pins setuptools>=65,<82, which is already within the needs_setuptools_pin safe range (>=62.3,<81 would be more conservative). We use the repo's own pin (setuptools>=65,<82) already expressed in pyproject dependencies — no extra step needed; uv sync --frozen will install the locked version.

nvidia-curobo requires CUDA devel toolkit at build time (CUDA C++ extension compilation). probe detected cuda_variant=runtime by default; overridden to devel via --cuda-variant devel. The Dockerfile must use the devel base image tag.

cuda_tag_source=hub-api: Docker Hub cuda:12.1.1 only has cudnn8 tags (not cudnn9). Using nvidia/cuda:12.1.1-cudnn8-devel-ubuntu22.04 as base image — this is correct despite probe reporting cudnn9 in probe.json.

ROBO_AUTO_ASSETS=1 (default) will run script/_download_assets.sh on first container start when assets are missing. This requires network and huggingface_hub; estimated ~10-20GB of assets. Surfaced as runtime_env_var so users can set ROBO_AUTO_ASSETS=0 to disable.
